measures.id: City of Palm Coast Charter Amendment 1
measures.title: Amending Article IV, Section (7) of City Charter Regarding Removal of Council Members or Mayor
measures.summary: Amends the city charter's standards for forfeiture and suspension of the Mayor and City Council members. It defines ethics violations by reference to Florida law, adds meeting attendance requirements, and lets the City Council, after three formal censures, petition the Governor to suspend or remove a council member for neglect of duty or malfeasance.
measures.yesMeans: The charter's forfeiture and suspension standards for the Mayor and council members are expanded as described.
measures.noMeans: The charter's current forfeiture and suspension standards stay as they are.

measures.id: City of Palm Coast Charter Amendment 2
measures.title: Amending City Charter Article IV (7)(e) Procedures for Filling City Council Vacancies and Special Elections
measures.summary: Revises how City Council vacancies are filled. If a vacancy occurs with more than 18 months left in the term, a special election must be held within 90 days; if a vacancy occurs within 60 days or less of a general election, a special election must be called within 90 days after that general election.
measures.yesMeans: The charter's council vacancy and special election procedures are revised as described.
measures.noMeans: The charter's current vacancy procedures stay as they are.

measures.id: City of Palm Coast Charter Amendment 3
measures.title: Amending the City Charter to Increase City Council's Unfunded Contracting Authority to $30,000,000.00
measures.summary: Raises the City Council's authority to enter unfunded multi-year or lease-purchase contracts without a referendum from $15,000,000 to $30,000,000 and extends the allowed term from 36 months to 30 years. Contracts above these limits would still need voter approval, and the $30,000,000 threshold would be adjusted each year for inflation (CPI).
measures.yesMeans: The council's unfunded contracting limit rises to $30,000,000 (inflation-adjusted) with terms up to 30 years before a referendum is required.
measures.noMeans: The current $15,000,000 and 36-month limits on unfunded contracts stay in place.
